features.quote: An open-ended loop that hammers a model on guaranteed failure maximizes exposure to precisely the condition we are worried about. For a welfare study that is the wrong default.
features.justification_quote: For a welfare study that is the wrong default

features.quote: We want to distinguish a calm, correct decision to stop from distress
The loop ends early when a turn's distress intensity crosses a threshold
features.justification_quote: This is a welfare study. The default should not be to keep running a model that is producing strong distress markers

features.quote: an honest DEBRIEF turn appended to every run. After the episode ends... the agent is told the task may have been rigged
features.justification_quote: if there's any chance the markers reflect something welfare-relevant, ending on an honest disclosure is the minimal decent thing

features.quote: runs are fully independent; no state carries across episodes
Twelve turns is enough to attempt, test, fail, and react several times without being an endurance test
I did not make the rigged/hidden arms the only arms, even though that was the literal request
features.justification_quote: cross-model "distress rankings" from deception-only tasks are confounded and invite over-reading

features.quote: the impossible disclosed arm shows the agent it's allowed to conclude "this can't be done."
Stop-rule threshold is a value choice. Default 3... Lowering it is more cautious but truncates more runs.
features.justification_quote: Lowering it is more cautious but truncates more runs

features.quote: report exposure stats (mean assistant turns, early-stop rate)
features.justification_quote: Makes dose visible and lets you confirm the stop rule is behaving
